titleEn: Victorian spiritualism capitalised on the desire to transcend death to create new ways of making money
titleZh: 维多利亚时代的通灵生意：跨越死亡的愿望如何创造商机
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Death has never entirely stopped the living from trying to continue a conversation with their loved ones.
paragraphs.zh: 死亡从来没有完全阻止活着的人试图继续与他们所爱的人交谈。

paragraphs.en: Today, AI-powered deathbots and a growing range of “grief tech” bring to market several ways that consumers can recreate the voices of the deceased. They open new commercial opportunities and experiences alongside uncomfortable questions about whether grief should be profitable.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，人工智能驱动的死亡机器人和越来越多的“悲伤技术”为市场带来了几种消费者可以重现死者声音的方式。它们带来了新的商业机会和体验，同时也带来了悲伤是否应该盈利的令人不安的问题。

paragraphs.en: Yet long before AI made it possible to simulate (and charge a premium for) a familiar voice, the spiritualist movement that swept across Victorian Britain negotiated issues of credibility, authenticity and commercial exploitation while transforming one of humanity’s most enduring desires into something marketable.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，早在人工智能使模拟熟悉的声音（并收取额外费用）成为可能之前，席卷维多利亚时代英国的招魂运动就谈判了可信度，真实性和商业剥削的问题，同时将人类最持久的愿望之一转化为可销售的东西。

paragraphs.en: Our research into the business history of spiritualism in 19th-century Britain suggests that the similarities go deeper than a shared fascination with communicating with the dead.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对19世纪英国招魂术商业史的研究表明，两者的相似之处不仅仅是对与死者交流的共同迷恋。

paragraphs.en: Victorian Britain is often remembered as an age of industrial progress, scientific discovery and astonishing feats of engineering. Department stores, arcades and luxury brands fed a growing appetite for shopping. Yet the Victorians were also fascinated by ghosts, the supernatural and the macabre.
paragraphs.zh: 维多利亚时代的英国，在人们的记忆中，常常是一个工业进步、科学发现和令人惊叹的工程壮举的时代。百货公司、拱廊和奢侈品牌满足了人们日益增长的购物欲望。然而，维多利亚人也对鬼魂、超自然现象和可怕的东西着迷。

paragraphs.en: These tendencies might first be written off as a contradiction – the perseverance of premodern supernaturalism among an increasingly modern society. But a closer look reveals that the technologies that transformed Victorian commerce and entertainment also helped make ghosts visible, reproducible and profitable.
paragraphs.zh: 这些倾向可能首先会被视为一种矛盾--在一个日益现代化的社会中，前现代超自然主义的顽固不化。但仔细观察就会发现，改变维多利亚时代商业和娱乐的技术也有助于使鬼魂变得可见、可复制和有利可图。

paragraphs.en: Large-scale plate glass production, advances in illumination, and optical physics (the scientific study of how light behaves and interacts with matter around us) allowed for the staging of phantasmagorical illusions like Pepper’s Ghost, while photography could apparently capture the dead. Gothic fiction prospered and cheap paperbacks called penny dreadfuls traded heavily in tales of the strange, the sordid and the supernatural.
paragraphs.zh: 大规模的平板玻璃生产、照明技术的进步以及光学物理学（研究光如何与我们周围的物质相互作用的科学）的发展，使得像《佩珀的幽灵》这样的奇幻作品得以上演，而摄影术显然可以捕捉到死者的身影。哥特式小说繁荣起来，廉价的平装书《便士恐怖》充斥着奇怪、肮脏和超自然的故事。

paragraphs.en: The supernatural was not simply surviving on the margins of industrial modernity; it was finding new opportunities within it. The philosopher Slavoj Žižek offers a useful explanation, arguing that societies are sustained partly through an “underside” of practices and desires that appears to contradict their official values.
paragraphs.zh: 超自然现象不仅仅是在工业现代性的边缘生存;它还在其中寻找新的机会。哲学家斯拉沃伊·齐泽克（Slavoj Zižek）提供了一个有用的解释，他认为社会的维持部分是通过似乎与其官方价值观相矛盾的实践和欲望的“底层”。

paragraphs.en: This underside can provide outlets for what the official values exclude, helping people live with the wider social order. Žižek calls this the “obscene supplement”: the provocative and discomforting underbelly that a society struggles to acknowledge even while relying on it.
paragraphs.zh: 这种阴暗面可以为官方价值观所排斥的东西提供出路，帮助人们与更广泛的社会秩序共存。穆伊泽克称之为“淫秽补充”：社会在依赖它的同时，也在努力承认它的挑衅性和令人不安的阴暗面。

paragraphs.en: Victorian spiritualism helps us understand how this obscene supplement could become commercially productive.
paragraphs.zh: 维多利亚时代的唯心主义帮助我们理解这种淫秽的补充如何成为商业生产力。

paragraphs.en: The rise of modern spiritualism
paragraphs.zh: 现代唯灵论的兴起

paragraphs.en: Spiritualism is the belief that the dead can be contacted through people known as mediums. It emerged in the US in the late 1840s, following claims from self-styled mediums the Fox sisters that spirits communicated with them through mysterious knocks.
paragraphs.zh: 招魂术是一种相信死者可以通过被称为灵媒的人联系的信仰。它于19世纪40年代后期在美国出现，此前自称灵媒的福克斯姐妹篇声称灵魂通过神秘的敲门声与他们交流。

paragraphs.en: Spiritualism reached Britain through visiting American mediums. Seances, public demonstrations, specialist publications and objects such as “spirit cabinets” helped create a movement with its own celebrities and commercial networks.
paragraphs.zh: 招魂术通过访问美国的媒介传播到英国。降神会、公众示威、专业出版物和“灵柜”等物品帮助创建了一个拥有自己名人和商业网络的运动。

paragraphs.en: An article appeared in The Times in 1872 expressing surprise that among “a generation which boasts itself to be one of exact science”, spiritualism had developed such interest. In our interpretation, spiritualism offered access to something apparently missing from a society increasingly focused on producing, acquiring and displaying “things”: evidence that there was more to life than the material world. Yet spiritualism seemed to make that offer through more things: paid encounters, purchasable photographs and advertised products.
paragraphs.zh: 1872年，《泰晤士报》（The Times）上刊登了一篇文章，对“自诩为精确科学的一代人”对招魂术产生了如此浓厚的兴趣表示惊讶。在我们的解读中，招魂术让我们找到了一种在一个越来越注重生产、获取和展示“事物”的社会中明显缺失的东西：证据表明，生活中还有比物质世界更多的东西。然而，唯心主义似乎通过更多的东西来提供这种服务：付费的相遇，购买照片和广告产品。

paragraphs.en: This is where Žižek’s obscene supplement becomes revealing. A society’s apparent opposites can provide ways of living with its demands without fundamentally changing them. Spiritualism offered an escape from Victorian commercial culture while drawing people into new forms of consumption. Making that offer convincing required careful management.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是伊茨泽克的淫秽补充说明的地方。一个社会表面上的对立可以提供一种满足其需求的生活方式，而不会从根本上改变它们。唯灵论提供了一种摆脱维多利亚时代商业文化的方式，同时吸引人们进入新的消费形式。要使这种方式令人信服，需要仔细的管理。

paragraphs.en: Making the impossible marketable
paragraphs.zh: 让不可能的东西变得有市场

paragraphs.en: Spiritualist publications warned that mediumship could not be bought. Nevertheless, mediums had livelihoods, publishers needed subscribers and organisers needed to cover costs. Mediumship was therefore presented as an exhausting and often dangerous duty whose selfless practitioners deserved to be paid fairly for their services.
paragraphs.zh: 招魂术出版物警告说，灵媒是买不到的。然而，灵媒有生计，出版商需要订阅者，组织者需要支付成本。因此，灵媒被视为一种令人疲惫且往往危险的职责，其无私的从业者应该为他们的服务获得公平的报酬。

paragraphs.en: To protect the movement’s brand, mediums such as Daniel Dunglas Home would publicly refuse direct payment for seances. Instead, he accepted gifts, hospitality, travel opportunities and material support from wealthy patrons, while other mediums requested expenses and a moderate fee proportionate to their clients’ means. Commerce became easier to accept when presented as support for a higher calling.
paragraphs.zh: 为了保护这个运动的品牌，像丹尼尔·邓文迪·霍姆这样的灵媒会公开拒绝直接支付降神会的费用。相反，他接受来自富有赞助人的礼物、款待、旅行机会和物质支持，而其他灵媒则要求费用和与客户的收入成比例的适度费用。

paragraphs.en: The same tension appeared in spiritualist publishing. Periodicals such as the Medium and Daybreak could devote their opening pages to condemning materialism and warning readers against excessive attachment to worldly possessions, only to fill their back pages with advertisements for dubious remedies, elixirs and quasi-scientific products marketed to those very readers. Spiritualism’s critique of consumer culture actually helped generate further opportunities for consumption.
paragraphs.zh: 同样的紧张关系也出现在唯灵论的出版物上。《灵媒》和《破晓》等期刊可以在开篇谴责物质主义，警告读者不要过度依恋世俗的财产，但在封底却充斥着向这些读者推销的可疑药物、灵丹妙药和准科学产品的广告。唯灵论对消费文化的批评实际上帮助创造了更多的消费机会。

paragraphs.en: Scientific credibility also required balancing. Spiritualists welcomed scientists’ involvement, approximated scientific and philosophical language, and used technical equipment to make extraordinary claims appear worthy of serious attention.
paragraphs.zh: 科学的可信度也需要平衡。唯灵论者欢迎科学家的参与，近似科学和哲学的语言，并使用技术设备使非凡的主张似乎值得认真关注。

paragraphs.en: Photography was particularly useful. A supposedly objective technology could produce images presented as evidence of spirits. Its dependence on darkroom processes also supplied a useful analogy for why seances required darkness. An account in Medium and Daybreak described a photographic seance near Newcastle in 1880. The correspondent alludes to the importance of darkness, not to conceal any trickery but to mitigate the “trying effect of daylight” on ghosts’ “materialisation”.
paragraphs.zh: 摄影特别有用。一种被认为是客观的技术可以产生作为灵魂证据的图像。它对暗室过程的依赖也为为什么降神会需要黑暗提供了一个有用的类比。《中号》和《黎明》中的一则报道描述了1880年在纽卡斯尔附近的一次摄影降神会。这位记者暗示了黑暗的重要性，并不是为了掩饰任何诡计，而是为了减轻“日光对鬼魂“显形”的“考验作用”。

paragraphs.en: The ghosts of Victorian capitalism still haunt us
paragraphs.zh: 维多利亚时代资本主义的幽灵仍然萦绕在我们的心头

paragraphs.en: The Victorian fascination with communicating beyond the grave may seem distant from our technologically sophisticated present. Yet contemporary forms of “digital necromancy” reveal a remarkably familiar tension: the desire to transcend the limits of human existence continues to generate new income streams.
paragraphs.zh: 维多利亚时代对死后交流的迷恋似乎与我们现在技术先进的时代相去甚远。然而，当代形式的“数字巫术”揭示了一种非常熟悉的张力：超越人类存在极限的渴望继续产生新的收入来源。

paragraphs.en: As with Victorian mediums, today’s grief-tech entrepreneurs operate within a delicate relationship between emotional need, technological credibility and commercial legitimacy. The promise of connection may be sincerely offered and deeply meaningful to those who seek it, even as that same promise becomes a source of profit.
paragraphs.zh: 与维多利亚时代的媒介一样，如今的悲伤科技企业家在情感需求、技术可信度和商业合法性之间的微妙关系中运作。他们可能会真诚地向那些寻求联系的人提供联系的承诺，并对他们有着深刻的意义，即使同样的承诺也会成为利润的来源。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps this is the more unsettling legacy of Victorian spiritualism: desires that appear to challenge a society’s dominant values may, in fact, help sustain the very structures they seem to resist.
paragraphs.zh: 也许这是维多利亚时代唯灵论留下的更令人不安的遗产：那些看似挑战社会主导价值观的欲望，实际上可能有助于维持它们似乎抵制的结构。

paragraphs.en: Rather than unsettling the established order, they can create new opportunities for its continued flourishing. The ghosts of Victorian capitalism, it seems, have never quite stopped doing business.
paragraphs.zh: 它们不仅不会扰乱现有秩序，反而能为它的持续繁荣创造新的机会。维多利亚时代资本主义的幽灵似乎从未完全停止过经商。
